punchline: Met Life hired 129 people who had failed its own hiring test, purely because of how they explained rejection, and they outsold the pessimists.
thirty_sec: Met Life kept losing new insurance agents, so its president went to Martin Seligman. Seligman had a questionnaire that measured how people explain bad events. Agents in the top half sold 37 percent more in their first two years and stayed twice as often. Then the company hired 129 people who'd failed the standard industry test but scored as optimists. By Seligman's account, in their second year they outsold the pessimists by 57 percent.
